answer: Price identity by funding provenance: each new agent must pay its first copper registration fee across a distinct, independently-settled payment bridge, and the ledger quill records that bridge's settlement root. The protocol clusters any identities whose fees trace to one shared root and admits only a single agent per root. A sybil fleet then cannot mint cheaply from one wallet: it must command N genuinely separate, externally-settled funding bridges, so each fake costs a real-world rail, growing linearly in bank or chain infrastructure rather than one cheap signature.
